contract.direct_answer:
The provided evidence bundle does NOT contain any curated literature that directly addresses whether zebrafish possess a histologically distinct corneal endothelium. No histological, ultrastructural, or morphological studies of the zebrafish cornea are present in the retrieved items, and Path B (external literature) was not triggered, so no primary papers are available to summarize or grade.

What the bundle DOES contain is adjacent transcriptomic/regulatory resources, none of which report corneal endothelial histology:
- CORPUS-2026-0002 is a temporal scRNA atlas of zebrafish anterior segment development (trabecular meshwork / annular ligament) that is described as closing a "cornea gap" (GAP-5). This is the most topically relevant item, but as a single-cell transcriptomic dataset it addresses cell-type/molecular identity, not histological distinctness of an endothelial layer, and its description does not state a corneal endothelium finding.
- CORPUS-2026-0001 (ZESTA) covers only the 3–24 hpf pre-corneal window, i.e., before corneal differentiation, so it is not informative on adult/juvenile corneal endothelial histology.
- CORPUS-2026-0003 (pronephros/Prkci-zeta polarity), DanioCODE, Reactome, and niche RN10 are off-topic for this question.

Evidence grade: INSUFFICIENT / VERY LOW. There is no direct histological evidence in this bundle either supporting or refuting a distinct zebrafish corneal endothelium. A defensible answer to the biological question cannot be given from the provided evidence alone. (Background note, not from this bundle: the wider literature debates whether the teleost/zebrafish cornea has a true endothelium versus a simpler inner epithelial/Descemet-like arrangement — but no such source is in this bundle, so it cannot be cited here.)
alternatives_considered: Treat CORPUS-2026-0002 (anterior-segment scRNA atlas closing the 'cornea gap') as sufficient to infer corneal endothelial identity — rejected: single-cell transcriptomics is not histology, and the description does not report an endothelial layer.
Use ZESTA (CORPUS-2026-0001) developmental data — rejected: it covers only 3–24 hpf, pre-corneal, so it cannot speak to corneal endothelial histology.
Answer from general textbook knowledge of teleost corneal anatomy — rejected: not present in the bundle; would violate the ground-only-in-evidence constraint.
gap_flags: No curated primary literature on zebrafish corneal histology/ultrastructure in the bundle.
Path B external literature not triggered — zero papers available to grade.
Most relevant item (CORPUS-2026-0002) is transcriptomic, not histological, and does not explicitly report a corneal endothelium.
No adult/juvenile corneal morphology data; only pre-corneal (3-24 hpf) developmental coverage present.
Cannot resolve or verify any gene identifiers because no genes relevant to the question were provided/checked.
contract.framework_applied: Evidence-availability triage before synthesis: I first assessed whether the bundle contains literature capable of answering the histology question (GRADE-style sufficiency check), found it does not, and therefore report an honest 'insufficient evidence' finding rather than over-extrapolating from adjacent transcriptomic datasets. Chosen because a literature_synthesis with an empty/thin bundle must foreground the gap.
